text.p: Italy's Chamber of Deputies (lower house) on Tuesday approved the government's controversial mini-budget after a confidence vote earlier swept away hundreds of opposition blocking amendments.

The house approved the bill by 287 votes to 214. Prime Minister Romano Prodi earlier comfortably won a confidence test called to speed up passage of the package, which the government says is key to its hopes of joining European monetary union.
The package, which is designed to cut 15.5 trillion lire ($9 billion) off this year's deficit, now goes to the Senate (upper house).
Prodi says the package is vital to enable Italy to meet the key three percent deficit-to-Gross Domestic Product ratio required for founder membership of the single currency in 1999. ($1=1,706 lire)
